summary.one_liner: A large community-maintained collection of practical Git command tips, each with a short description and a copy-pasteable command, plus alternatives.
summary.what_it_does: The README is an organized list of roughly 300 Git tips grouped into sections: Basic Operations, Branching, Log and History, Merging and Rebasing, Miscellaneous, Remotes, Setup and Config, Stashing, Submodules and Subtrees, Tagging, and Undoing Changes. Each tip gives a one-line goal and a shell command, and many add alternative commands. Examples include finding the commit where a bug was introduced with git bisect, sparse checkout, shallow and partial clones, bundles for offline sharing, signing commits with an SSH key, and enabling rerere for recurring merge conflicts. The README says the commands were tested on git 2.7.4 and points to a GitBook version and a git-tip CLI that runs in a Docker container. Translations in several languages are linked at the top.
use_cases: Look up a Git command for a specific task
Undo or revert commits and local changes
Clean up merged or stale branches
Search Git history for a bug or a change
Set up Git config and aliases
notable: Covers about 300 tips organized by topic with alternative commands for many of them
Commands were tested on git 2.7.4 per the README, so newer or older versions may differ
Includes modern equivalents such as git switch and git restore next to classic commands
Available in many languages, with a linked interactive GitBook version
Companion git-tip CLI runs in a Docker container
caveats: Tested only on git 2.7.4 according to the README, so some commands may behave differently on current Git
Several tips are destructive (force push, reset --hard, filter-branch) and need care
The README does not state a license
